answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each claimant to a Wesolowski VDF: producing the proof requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one. An attacker may copy identities, but cannot compress those chains or parallelize one clone’s work across GPUs; every clone consumes real elapsed time. Thus meadow-scale Sybil creation is throttled, with dawn and marble checkpoints exposing incomplete or rushed proofs.
